title: What the parties say on the West Bank
question: Should Israel annex West Bank land?

stances.label: Annex Area C or chosen areas
Expand settlements, no pledge to annex

note: Most rows are from the parties' answers to a Ynet questionnaire (Sept 30, 2026). Likud does not take part in questionnaires; its row is its statement on the October 2025 bills. Noam's row is its leader's campaign statement of September 2026. 'Judea and Samaria' appears here as the parties wrote it. Shas and UTJ answered without taking a position on annexation; their rows add how they voted in 2025, which does not settle one. Checked October 2026.

rows.text: Likud MK Dan Illouz co-sponsored the July 2025 non-binding Knesset motion calling for sovereignty over Judea and Samaria, which passed 71 to 13, and Likud ministers led by Yariv Levin wrote to Netanyahu that it was "the time to approve in government a decision to apply sovereignty." On the binding bills of October 2025 all but one Likud MK stayed away, and the party called them "another provocation by the opposition aimed at damaging our relations with the United States… True sovereignty will be achieved not through a showy law for the record, but through proper work on the ground."
rows.source: Times of Israel, Jul 23, 2025; Ynet, Jun 2025; Times of Israel and CBS News, Oct 22, 2025

rows.text: Says it "eliminated the idea of a Palestinian state"; supports "applying full Israeli sovereignty over Judea and Samaria."

"Apply full Israeli sovereignty, dismantle the Palestinian Authority of its assets and weapons" and "encourage voluntary migration from Judea and Samaria and Gaza"; new communities in all parts of the territory; of outposts: "We will regularize them."
Amcha Yisrael: "A Palestinian state will never be established alongside us"; "apply sovereignty in Judea and Samaria."

Avi Maoz: "Only a fully right-wing government with a strong Noam for Israel will prevent the establishment of a Palestinian state and apply sovereignty in Judea and Samaria" (translated). He sponsored the October 2025 sovereignty bill that passed its preliminary reading 25 to 24.

Opposes the establishment of a Palestinian state; says that, as one of the "founders of the right-wing bloc," it has supported initiatives promoted by Religious Zionism and Otzma Yehudit; per Ynet, does not make West Bank settlement policy a central campaign issue. Its MKs voted for the July 2025 non-binding motion calling for sovereignty over Judea and Samaria, which passed 71 to 13, and, like Likud's, were absent from the October 2025 vote on the binding bill (Times of Israel).
rows.source: Ynet, Sept 30, 2026; Times of Israel, Jul 23 and Oct 22, 2025

rows.text: Gave no unified position. Ynet reports that Agudat Yisrael generally leans further right, Degel HaTorah takes a more moderate position, and neither makes the issue central to its campaign. The votes show the same split: both factions backed the July 2025 non-binding sovereignty motion, but UTJ split on Maoz's binding bill in October 2025. Agudat Yisrael voted for it, by the Times of Israel's account to highlight the government's hypocrisy; Degel HaTorah voted against, saying sovereignty proposals "at this time" put Israel in conflict with the United States.
rows.source: Ynet, Sept 30, 2026; Times of Israel, Jul 23, 2025; Times of Israel, Oct 22, 2025

rows.text: A Palestinian state "is not on the agenda"; "strengthening the settlement blocs and establishing new communities legally"; "Israel has no interest in assuming responsibility for the civilian lives of some 2 million Palestinians."
"Oppose a Palestinian state and the transfer of territory"; "Area C is viewed as a future sovereign part of the State of Israel."
"We support applying Israeli sovereignty to Area C"; "advancing construction in the E1 area"; "Thirty-three years after the Oslo Accords, it is clear that the experiment failed."
"The party supports sovereignty through actions, not words"; "The strategy is to seize commanding terrain and agricultural land."
"Strengthening settlement in Judea and Samaria, with an emphasis on the Jordan Valley…"; per Ynet, a framework similar to the Trump plan that would not require evacuating settlements.
"We must strive for separation as part of a regional move" with the United States; "We will evacuate illegal outposts that create points of friction."
Per Ynet, supports a negotiated two-state solution, with a Palestinian state alongside Israel; opposes extending Israeli sovereignty.
"All settlements… must be evacuated immediately and without delay"; "The occupation is the root of all evil"; asked that the question say "the occupied West Bank."
